conditions.exact_rule_quote: sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises
conditions.description: The tenant must have sub-let, assigned, or otherwise parted with possession of the whole or any part of the premises.
conditions.scope: Delhi Rent Control Act section 14(1)(b); fixed subletting/assignment/parting-with-possession issue.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: on or after the 9th day of June, 1952
conditions.description: The relevant subletting, assignment, or parting with possession must have occurred on or after 9 June 1952.
conditions.scope: Temporal limit in Delhi Rent Control Act section 14(1)(b); the pre-9 June 1952 deeming rule in section 16(1) is outside the alleged 1992/2008 chronology.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord
conditions.description: The relevant subletting, assignment, or parting with possession must have occurred without written landlord consent; section 16(3) additionally states the requirement as previous consent in writing after commencement of the Act.
conditions.scope: Written-consent condition for the same relevant transfer or parting with possession; no implied-consent rule is added.

bindings.reason: The petitioners' claimed original letting to the respondent supplies the asserted baseline tenant identity against which any later transfer of possession to the firms would be assessed.
The petitioners directly allege subletting to two firms carrying on business independently, which is candidate evidence for parting with possession but is not itself an established fact.
The respondent's two-distinct-tenancies account tends to defeat the proposition that one tenancy was later parted with to third parties.

The respondent's own pleading places each firm in tenancy and possession of a separate shop, providing candidate evidence of possession by persons or firms other than the asserted original tenant, while leaving the legal character disputed.
The respondent's claimed participation as partner in both firms is candidate evidence that he retained participation or control, which tends against complete divestment of possession.

The respondent's account of a pre-2008 single tenancy later divided into two tenancies is candidate evidence of a change in possessory or tenancy arrangement, although the respondent characterizes that change as lawful new tenancies.
The respondent dates the alleged separation and creation of two tenancies to March 2008, which is after the statutory cutoff.
The respondent likewise places the asserted division into two tenancies in 2008, supporting the temporal condition if that is the legally relevant arrangement.
The petitioners expressly allege that no written permission was obtained for the alleged subletting.
The respondent alleges landlord consent and a written understanding dated 10.03.2008, directly contesting the absence-of-written-consent condition, subject to authenticity, timing, and legal effect.

target_refs.quote: first ingredient of Sec. 14(1)(b) of D.R.C. Act is satisfied as the physical as well as legal possession of the tenanted premises has been parted with

element_targets.reason: The target court expressly adopted the first section 14(1)(b) ingredient and found parting with both physical and legal possession.

target_refs.quote: Sh. Ramji Lal Goel and Sh. Bhajan Lal Goel got retired from the firm w.e.f. 01.04.1992
the physical as well as legal possession of the tenanted premises has been parted with

element_targets.reason: The target court accepted a 1992 retirement fact in the reasoning immediately preceding its express finding of parting with possession; 1992 is after the statutory cutoff of 9 June 1952.

target_refs.quote: no cogent and convincing evidence documentary or oral has been produced before this court which prove that such consent in writing was given
ingredient in respect of not taking of consent of landlord in writing is also satisfied

element_targets.reason: The target court expressly found the no-written-consent ingredient satisfied because the respondent did not produce cogent and convincing proof of written consent; this is labeled burden not carried rather than a finding that the asserted writing never existed.

target_refs.quote: the ingredients of 14(1)(b) D.R.C. Act are satisfied and consequently, an eviction order is passed

issue_target.reason: The target court expressly held that the section 14(1)(b) ingredients were satisfied and granted relief on that ground.

gaps.description: The frozen input inventory reports that partnership deeds and bank records were produced but expressly omits their substantive contents and court assessment. The target court's first-ingredient reasoning relies materially on contents later described from those records, including the 1992 retirement and bank-operation evidence. Those target-only factual propositions cannot be added to bindings without violating input/target isolation.

The frozen input contains the respondent's claim of a 10.03.2008 written understanding but does not contain the evidentiary details later used by the target court to assess that document's provenance, timing, or probative force. The target label for written consent is therefore learnable as an outcome label, but the full target application rationale is not reconstructible from existing input facts alone.
